**Review: Instagram draft, Pebblebrook Tea Co.**

**Claims list**

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "New tins just landed for winter" | OK. New arrivals are fine as written. |
| "Deep green, gold lettering" | OK. Product fact. |
| "planet-friendly packaging" | **Unsupported.** Vague environmental claim. The allowlist only covers plastic-free, home compostable tea bags. Nothing backs the tins or other packaging as "planet-friendly". In the UK, vague green claims like this are a regulatory risk (CMA Green Claims Code, ASA). |
| "the same plastic-free tea bags inside" | Allowlisted. |
| "Our tea bags are plastic-free and home compostable" | Allowlisted. |

**Other notes**
- The last sentence repeats "plastic-free" from the sentence before it. Merging them gives a tighter post.
- No ban-list words, no fake urgency, no invented stats or testimonials.

**Suggested compliant version**

> New tins just landed for winter. Deep green, gold lettering, and the same plastic-free, home compostable tea bags inside.

If you want to say something about the tin itself being eco-friendly (recyclable, reusable, and so on), send me the specific fact and its source. I can then add it in place of "planet-friendly". For now: `[PROOF NEEDED: what makes the tin packaging better for the environment]`.
